questions.q: Which check is a rule for @zudojs/validation rather than a shape for the task's @zudojs/schema DTO?
questions.explain: Types, formats, allowed values and defaults describe the shape of one value. "The same title ignoring case and spacing" depends on what the value means and on the other tasks: a rule, checked after the schema has produced a typed value.
options: The priority is one of low, normal, high
No two tasks may have titles that differ only in case and spacing

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: trim() only removes spaces at the ends, so " Buy milk " joins "Buy milk". The double space and the capitals still make two more distinct strings.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Each emoji is two UTF-16 code units, so length is 4 and the schema's min(3) passes. The constraint counts code points, what a person sees: 2 characters, so it fails.

questions.q: An error handler checks isSchemaValidationError(error) from @zudojs/schema before adding issues to the response. What happens with an error thrown by parse from @zudojs/validation?
questions.explain: The two packages have different error classes. They share status and code, so generic handling works, but a guard from one package does not recognise the other's errors.
options: It is recognised, because both have the code ERR_SCHEMA_VALIDATION
It is not recognised, so the issues are not added; the error is still an exposed 400

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: checkConstraints runs every constraint and collects every failure, each with the path you passed, so a form can show all problems at once.

questions.q: Why does checkConstraint not copy the rejected value into the issue?
questions.explain: An error that echoes "hunter2 is too short" leaks the password to anyone reading the response or the logs. The code and message are enough to fix the input.
options: Issues end up in exposed 400 responses and in logs, and the rejected value may be a password, a token or personal data
So that the same issue can be reused for many values

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: httpUrl accepts only http: and https:. A javascript: link in a profile would run script when clicked; an ftp: link is not what a web profile expects either.

questions.q: What is the guard option of createConstraint for?
questions.explain: Constraints often receive raw request data. Without a guard, value.length on a number throws, and a 400 becomes a 500.
options: It makes the constraint run only in production
It checks the value's type first, so a wrong-typed value from a request is an ordinary failure instead of a TypeError inside your function

options:

questions.q: Why might you prefer checkConstraints([integer, between(1, 8)], value) over checkConstraint(combineConstraints(integer, between(1, 8)), value)?
questions.explain: combineConstraints fails with "One or more validation constraints failed." When the user needs to know what to fix, keep the rules separate.
options: The combined constraint reports one generic message; the list reports which rules failed
The combined constraint ignores the second rule
The list stops at the first failure

questions.q: A service checks "no control characters" on the raw title, then stores cleanTitle(raw). What is wrong with that order?
questions.explain: Validate the exact value you keep. If normalization changes the value after the check, the check says nothing about the stored data.
options: Nothing; the order does not matter
The check approved a different value than the one stored; always normalize first, then check what you will store

questions.q: Why does the Task API store titles in NFC but compare them with an NFKC-based key?
questions.explain: NFC only merges different encodings of the same character, so it is safe for storage. NFKC turns Ｂｕｙ into Buy and ﬁ into fi: exactly what uniqueness needs, but not what you should show the user as their title.
options: NFC keeps what the user typed while unifying identical-looking encodings; NFKC also folds compatibility forms like fullwidth letters, which is right for deciding sameness but changes the text
NFC removes accents and NFKC keeps them

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The first three share the key pay rent; the exclamation mark makes a genuinely different title. The clean form keeps the user's capitals and only collapses and trims spaces.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Only the domain is lower-cased. The part before @ may be case-sensitive by the e-mail standards, and folding it could merge two different mailboxes.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: toLowerCase is a display transform and leaves ß alone. Case folding for comparison maps ß and SS to the same form.
questions.code:
import { foldCase } from "@zudojs/validation";

console.log("STRASSE".toLowerCase() === "Straße".toLowerCase(), foldCase("STRASSE") === foldCase("Straße"));

questions.q: Why does createValidationComposer stop at the first failing step by default?
questions.explain: If step 1 found that the amount is not a number, step 2 checking "at most ₦20,000" on it produces noise. Set stopOnFirstError: false only for independent checks.
options: Steps usually build on each other; a later step would check a value an earlier step already found broken
Because only one issue can be reported

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: when runs the step only when the predicate matches, so the ₦20,000 cap applies to USSD transfers only.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: assert throws a ConstraintValidationError, an exposed 400 whose message names the composer. The detailed issues are on the error's issues.
options: RangeError 400 Value must be between 1 and 30.
ConstraintValidationError 422 Value must be between 1 and 30.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default, like @zudojs/schema. The client's discount never reaches your code.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: parseOr returns the parsed value, or the fallback when validation fails, for both a non-number and an out-of-range number.

questions.q: A Zod schema has an asynchronous refine ("is this username free?"). What does the synchronous validate from @zudojs/validation do with it?
questions.explain: Zod cannot run an asynchronous rule synchronously and throws. validateAsync and parseAsync run it properly.
options: Throws a plain Error, which a server would answer with 500; use validateAsync

questions.q: An asynchronous rule checks that a username is free before the insert. Why is that not enough to guarantee unique usernames?
questions.explain: Check-then-act is a race. The rule gives a friendly message in the common case; the database constraint is the real guarantee.
options: Two requests can both pass the check before either inserts; only a unique index in the database guarantees it
The check only looks at the first 10 users

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The message lists every issue with its path, so a handler that only sends message still tells the client what to fix.
options: 400 title: Must be at least 3 characters; priority: Must be low, normal or high
422 title: Must be at least 3 characters

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: toJSON, which loggers and error handlers use, replaces the value with its type and length. The in-memory issue still has it, so never log error.issues directly.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The same object used twice is a shared reference, which serializes fine. Only a value that leads back to itself is a cycle.

questions.q: Why is CircularReferenceError a 500, while SerializationDepthError from the depth guard is a 400?
questions.explain: A request body is JSON, which can nest but cannot refer back to itself. Cycles show up in outgoing data such as ORM objects, which is your responsibility.
options: Cycles are more dangerous than deep nesting
JSON.parse cannot create a cycle, so a cycle comes from data your code built, a bug; too-deep JSON comes from the client
Because cycles cannot be detected quickly

questions.q: assertSizeWithinLimit(body, 65_536) estimates two bytes per UTF-16 code unit. What does that mean for a title of Chinese characters or ₦ signs?
questions.explain: For ASCII the estimate is about double the real size, for three-byte UTF-8 characters it is about two thirds. The guard is a cheap structural check, not a byte limit.
options: The estimate is always higher than the real size, so the guard is strict
Those characters take three bytes in UTF-8, so the estimate is too low and a larger body can pass; keep the server's byte limit as the hard cap
The estimate is exact for every script

questions.q: A stored task fails its response schema. What should the client get?
questions.explain: The client did nothing wrong, and the failing fields describe your internal data. It is a server bug: answer 500, log the details, fix the data.
options: 400 with the list of failing fields
A generic 500; the details go to the log
200 with the invalid task, because the client asked for it

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The response schema is an allow-list, so the password hash never leaves. A failure becomes an unexposed 500, so the client learns nothing about the internal data.

questions.q: In the Task API's update, why does assertUniqueTitle(title, id) skip the task being updated?
questions.explain: A change of capitals or spacing is a rename of the same task, not a duplicate of another one.
options: Renaming "buy milk" to "Buy milk" gives the same key as the task itself; without skipping it, the task would conflict with itself
Because updated tasks cannot have duplicates
Because the store does not contain the task during an update

questions.q: Where does the lesson put the title rules, and why not in the DTO schema?
questions.explain: The generated validators/ folder is meant for such rules. The service calls them after the schema, so every path that creates or renames a task uses the same rules.
options: In src/routes/, because rules are HTTP concerns
In src/validators/tasks.rules.ts; the DTO describes the shape of input, while the rules (normalization, sameness, characters) are used by the service for creates and updates alike
In src/utils/http.ts, next to the JSON guards

questions.q: Write hasControlCharacter(text) that is true when the text contains any Unicode control character (\p{Cc}), and cleanThenCheck(raw) that first collapses every run of whitespace to one space and trims, and then returns "ok" or "control character".
questions.explain: Tabs and newlines are whitespace and are cleaned away first, so they do not count. Other control characters, such as the bell or NUL, survive cleaning and are refused. Checking after cleaning means you check what you store.
questions.expected:
"Buy milk" ok
"Buy\tmilk\n" ok
"Pay rent\u0007" control character
"\u0000Book plumber" control character

questions.q: Write titleKey(title) using only built-ins: NFKC normalization (normalize("NFKC")), collapse whitespace, trim, and lower-case. Then write findDuplicates(titles) returning the titles whose key was already seen.
questions.explain: Every spelling of the same title maps to one key, so a Set of keys finds duplicates. @zudojs/validation's normalizeIdentifier uses case folding instead of toLowerCase, which also handles cases such as ß.

questions.q: Using @zudojs/validation, create a constraint nigerianPhone with code invalid_phone and message Enter a number like 0803 123 4567, accepting 11 digits starting with 0 after removing spaces. Check the three numbers with checkConstraint and print whether each passed.
questions.explain: A custom constraint is a function plus a name, a code and a message. The guard keeps a non-string from reaching replace, so bad input is a failure, not a crash.

questions.q: Write your own tiny composer: compose(steps, stopOnFirst) returns a function that runs each step (a function returning a list of messages) and returns all messages, or only the first failing step's messages when stopOnFirst is true.
questions.explain: Stopping at the first failure suits steps that build on each other; collecting everything suits independent checks. createValidationComposer offers the same choice with stopOnFirstError.
questions.expected:
[ 'whole kobo only' ]
[ 'whole kobo only', 'USSD limit is ₦20,000' ]

questions.q: Write an iterative depthOf(value, limit) that returns the nesting depth of arrays and plain objects (primitives are 0, [] is 1), and stops and returns limit + 1 as soon as the depth passes limit. Use an explicit stack, not recursion, so hostile input cannot overflow the call stack.
questions.explain: A recursive walk would overflow on the 100,000-level array before it could report anything, so the guard must be iterative and must stop as soon as the limit is passed. That is how the structural guards in @zudojs/validation are built.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A registry stores rules by name. The string "3" is not coerced: the constraints' guards report a wrong type as an ordinary failure rather than crashing.

questions.q: A project already describes every request body with Zod. Which approach fits ZudoJS best?
questions.explain: Describing the same DTO in two schema systems means two definitions that drift apart. @zudojs/validation exists partly for this case, and its z re-export avoids a second Zod.
options: Rewrite every DTO in @zudojs/schema and keep the Zod ones as well
Keep Zod and use it through @zudojs/validation's validate/parse and its re-exported z, so results and errors have the ZudoJS shapes
Install a second copy of Zod next to the one @zudojs/validation uses
Validate by hand, because the packages cannot be mixed

questions.q: Which check belongs to request validation rather than response validation?
questions.explain: Depth limits protect the server from hostile input, which only arrives in requests. The other three protect clients from your own data.
options: Dropping an internal ownerId before a task is sent
Detecting a cycle between an order and its customer before serializing
Refusing a body nested 1000 levels deep with 400
Turning a stored task with done: "no" into a 500

questions.q: Write fieldErrors(issues): for issues with a path and a message, return an object with one message per top-level field (the first path segment), keeping the first message for each field, and using "(form)" for issues with an empty path.
questions.explain: Using Object.hasOwn instead of field in errors matters: in would find the inherited constructor and silently drop that field's message. toFieldErrors in @zudojs/validation avoids the same trap.
